title: Poincaré limit cycles and the theory of self-sustaining oscillations (Les cycles limites de Poincaré et la théorie des oscillations autoentretenues)
kind: primary-paper (English translation of the French original)
relevance: Primary precedent for 'self-sustaining oscillation' as a physical-unity concept: non-conservative systems sustaining oscillations by drawing energy from non-periodic sources; self-oscillations correspond to stable Poincaré limit cycles with amplitude and period independent of initial conditions; amplitude balance integral (C) and stability condition (D) are the ancestors of the gain-loss throughput used in RESULT.md §2/§4.
limits: 2-page Comptes Rendus note read in full via the ICT Open University classics translation; page/line numbering of the French original not collated; the small-parameter perturbation calculation (eq. B-D) is read at statement level, not re-derived term by term.
version: Comptes rendus de l'Académie des Sciences 189 (1929), pp. 559-561; translation hosted by ICT Open University Classics (accessed 2026-10-31, 139,790 B PDF, 2 pages).
section_locator: Sec. 1 (energy from non-periodic sources); Sec. 2 (stable Poincaré limit cycles; period and amplitude independent of initial conditions); Sec. 3 eqs. (B)-(D) (small-mu normal-form precursor with amplitude balance integral and stability inequality); Sec. 4.
assumptions: Planar autonomous ODEs (A); the perturbed-rotation family (B) with small real parameter mu; stability w.r.t. initial conditions and w.r.t. equation perturbations.
conclusion: Paper authors' claim: self-sustaining oscillations of one-degree-of-freedom systems correspond mathematically to stable Poincaré limit cycles; the theory is thereby put on rigorous footing in the simplest case.
proof_status: Established classic; statement-level correspondence checked directly by this lane against the translation; no re-derivation of the perturbation series.
dependencies: Poincaré, Les méthodes nouvelles de la mécanique céleste (1892) (cited, not read)
Lyapunov stability memoir (cited, not read)
open_questions: The later Andronov-Vitt phase-stability theorem (neutral phase direction plus decaying amplitude) was not accessed directly this lane; RESULT.md §4(c)-(d) cites its printed descendant in Pietras-Daffertshofer eqs. (4.22)-(4.23) instead.

The lane re-derives nothing beyond these printed statements; no mathematical novelty is claimed against this source.
version: Physics Reports 819 (2019) 1-105, DOI 10.1016/j.physrep.2019.06.001; received 2 July 2018, accepted 4 June 2019, available online 25 June 2019; author-hosted open-access PDF (3,871,563 B, 113 PDF pages = 105 printed pages) fetched 2026-10-31.
section_locator: Sec. 2.1 (pp. 9-10): asymptotic phase and isochrons, refs to Guckenheimer 1975 [91] and Wiggins [92]; Sec. 4.2 (p. 18-19) eq. (4.4) M-th order Hopf normal form and its M=2 Stuart-Landau form w' = alpha w - beta |w|^2 w with alpha=u0+iv0, beta=u1+iv1, radius R = sqrt(u0/u1); Sec. 4.4 (pp. 22-24): polar dynamics eq. (4.18) with R' = R*Re, theta' = Im decoupled; cycle w_c(t) = R_c e^{i omega t}, R_c = sqrt(u0/u1), omega = v0 - v1 c2, c2 = u0/u1, T = 2pi/omega; printed asymptotic phase map Theta(w = R e^{i phi}) = arg w - (v1/u1) ln(|w|/R_c); linearized deviations eqs. (4.21)-(4.23) with eigenvalues lambda_0 = 0 and lambda_1 = -2 s_R (s_R = u0); phase sensitivity function eqs. (4.20)/(4.25); Sec. 11.2 (isostables, augmented phase reduction).
assumptions: Smooth planar dynamics near a supercritical Hopf bifurcation; normal-form truncation at order M (residual O_{2M}(w)); real bifurcation parameter mu as distance to the Hopf point; hyperbolically stable limit cycle.
conclusion: Paper authors' claim: analytic phase reduction via the Hopf normal form yields identical reduced phase dynamics across isochron (Winfree), Floquet (Kuramoto), adjoint, and averaging methods, with explicit parameter expressions; phase-amplitude extensions track the transverse dynamics.
proof_status: Peer-reviewed review with derivations in appendices; this lane verified the M=2, real-beta special case by exact rational arithmetic (RESULT.md §9) and read the printed general formulas directly; no independent audit of the general-M proofs.

title: Biological organisation as closure of constraints
kind: primary-paper (process/organizational-closure theory; author-deposited HAL copy of the published article)
relevance: Primary process-unity precedent read before any original interpretation: Definition 1 (constraint: asymmetric causal action plus temporal symmetry at the same time scale), Definition 4 (closure: each constraint dependent and generative, strict closure indivisible), footnote 14 (a time scale is a relaxation exponential t -> exp(-t/tau) — the exact concept of RESULT.md's restoration rate, distinguished from process durations), and footnote 25 (an explicit denial that a mere cycle of processes, e.g. the hydrologic cycle, is a unity). Grounds both the U-criterion comparison and the brief's caution that not every stable cycle is a genuine unity.
limits: Full text read except that the lane did not reconstruct their formal apparatus beyond Definitions 1-4 and the cited passages; the lane does not claim the Stuart-Landau system realizes closure (parameters model an unmodeled pump/bath, which their constraint ontology does not straightforwardly license); no attribution of the U-criterion to Montévil-Mossio.
version: Journal of Theoretical Biology 372 (2015) 179-191, DOI 10.1016/j.jtbi.2015.02.029; HAL hal-01192916v1 (author manuscript deposited 3 Sep 2015; 29 PDF pages), fetched 2026-10-31 from hal.sorbonne-universite.fr.
section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 1 (self-determination; Piaget openness/closure; autopoiesis; Rosen closure to efficient causation); Sec. 2 (self-constraint); Sec. 3 Definition 1 (constraint) with discussion; footnote 14 (time scale as relaxation exponential; time scale vs overall duration); Sec. 4 Definitions 2-3 (dependence, direct dependence; slow/fast dependence); Sec. 5 Definition 4 (overall/strict closure); footnote 25 (closure vs mere cycle of processes; hydrologic-cycle example); Sec. 6.1-6.2 (tendency to closure; hierarchical boundaries); Sec. 7 (invariance and variation; closure described over a temporal interval, 'extracted from the dynamics ... in physical time', p. 19).
assumptions: Biological organization as mutual dependence among constraints conserved (symmetric) w.r.t. the processes they channel, at stated time scales; thermodynamic openness held distinct from organizational closure.
conclusion: Paper authors' claim: closure of constraints characterizes biological organization; closure grounds functionality and boundaries; it is a stabilizing invariant described over a temporal interval, not at an instant.
proof_status: Conceptual/formal framework published in a peer-reviewed journal; this lane uses only their definitions and explicit disclaimers, checked against the deposited text.
dependencies: Rosen, Life Itself (1991) (cited, not read)
Moreno & Mossio, Biological Autonomy (2015) (cited, not read this lane)
Kauffman, Investigations (2002) work-constraint cycle (cited, not read)
open_questions: Whether a two-element gain-loss organization with an unmodeled pump can ever satisfy their Definition 4 is left open here; RESULT.md §3 deliberately does not claim it.

title: How Thick is Now? The Prospects of Thick Presentism
relevance: Strongest contrary evidence recorded in RESULT.md §8: surveys the motivation for a temporally extended present (Zeno/change, causation, temporal experience) and argues that all four thick-presentist views (with/without real times x with/without overlap) are untenable; records Hestevold's temporal atom ('a butterfly flapping its wings exactly twice', Hestevold 2008 p. 334 as quoted on Backmann p. 105) — literally a cycle-duration present, i.e. the direct precedent for the cycle-selection rival R2; supplies the ordering/overlap dilemma any cycle-present proposal inherits.
limits: All 11 pages read (published pagination 99-119). The lane takes Backmann's exposition of Hestevold 2008, Baron 2012, McKinnon 2003, Orilia 2012, Dainton 2001 at his reported depth; those primaries were not independently accessed (separate discovery records where cited). The lane does not adjudicate his negative conclusion; it records the dilemma as standing contrary evidence.
version: Metaphysica 26 (2025), published online 24 December 2025; journal listing Metaphysica 2026; 27(1): 99-119; DOI 10.1515/mp-2025-0006; received 19 Feb 2025, accepted 12 Aug 2025; University of Bayreuth open-access copy (665,930 B, 11 PDF pages) fetched 2026-10-31. (Author deceased September 2025; correspondence via Johanna Thoma per the paper's note.)
section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 1 (dynamic change, McTchange); Sec. 2 (arguments for temporal extension: Le Poidevin on Zeno's arrow; change over intervals; Baron on causation; James/Russell on temporal experience); Sec. 3.1.1 (Hestevold's limited time-free thick presentism; temporal-atom quotation p. 105; Orilia's precedence/McTaggart-principle objection; McKinnon's no-order objection); Sec. 3.1.2 (Baron's timed overlap; Dainton on transitivity of coexistence; compresentness explosion vs hyper-progression); Sec. 3.2 (no-overlap views; stuttering change); Sec. 4 conclusions (all four views fail); references (Hestevold 2008, Pacific Philosophical Quarterly 89: 325-347; Baron 2012, Philosophical Papers 41(1): 1-21; McKinnon 2003, Australasian Journal of Philosophy 81: 305-323; Orilia 2012, Philosophical Studies 160: 407-414; Dainton 2001).
assumptions: Presentism as the frame; thick present = present with duration; the four-fold logical space defined by (times real?) x (overlap?).
conclusion: Paper authors' claim: none of the four possible thick-presentist positions is tenable; extending the present multiplies rather than solves the problems of change, causation, motion, and experience.
proof_status: Published philosophical argument, read in full; correctness not independently adjudicated by this lane; used here as the strongest standing objection, not as settled truth.
dependencies: Hestevold 2008 (discovery; see cc-hestevold-2008)
Baron 2012 (discovery; see cc-baron-2012)
McKinnon 2003 (discovery; see cc-mckinnon-2003)
Orilia 2012 (discovery, within this record)
Dainton 2001, Time and Space (discovery, within this record)
open_questions: Whether a dynamical (phase-ordered) internal-time reply to his ordering dilemma exists is listed as proposed next task 3 in RESULT.md §12; not answered here.
